notes: Account summary: QLT is a fintech analytics platform. Heavy in realtime chat assistants for traders + nightly batch reranks for signals. Looking for predictable unit economics and strong isolation.
Primary ask: Dedicated pool with throughput guarantees and latency SLOs for realtime chat routes. Wants explicit reserved GPU planning for peak market open windows.

Throughput targets called out on call: baseline 1.2k req/s @ 64 tokens for chat during normal hours; peak 3k req/s bursts for market-open spikes (5-10 min windows). Background rerank jobs 200-400 qps but can be lower priority.
Latency SLA: customer insists on p95 latency target for chat <= 250ms for 64-token responses. Will accept higher p95 for batch/rerank. Wants latency SLOs tied to credits in contract.

Reserved GPU ask: initial committed pool equivalent to 12x A100-80GB or 24x A100-40GB (SE recommended L40s as alternate). Wants sizing worksheet from Redwood with token/sec mapping and KV cache assumptions.
Traffic shaping / priority lanes requirements (key topic):
- Two priority lanes: realtime-chat (non-preemptible except by infra emergency) and background (preemptible).
- Per-route quotas: ability to set qps/token caps per route and per API key. Burst windows with token-burst budget for market-open spikes.
- Tenant isolation: strict noisy-neighbor controls, accounting by tenant+route, and isolated GPU tenancy for critical lanes if required.
- Noisy neighbor mitigation: automatic detection (tail-latency spikes), circuit-breaker to throttle or quarantine offending workloads, and alerting to QLT ops.
- Preemption policy: graceful preemption for lower-priority lanes with configurable drain timeout and retry/fallback to hosted smaller models.
Quoted buyer: 'If we lose market-open latency for even 2 minutes, it's a major revenue hit — need hard guarantees or automatic fallback to cheaper replicas.'
SLA negotiation points: target 99.95% uptime for Dedicated control plane, separate latency SLOs per route; credit calculus must include market-open critical windows.
Fallbacks & routing: wants automated fallback to a compatible quantized/cheaper model variant under sustained overload, plus region-fallback for EU residency cases.
Observability requests: token-level cost/latency breakdowns per route, per-API-key tracing, and per-priority lane dashboards. Retention 90 days for audit signals.
Security & compliance: must pass iso27001 evidence, support customer-managed KMS, SSO/SAML, and EU data residency for EU customers. Legal expects standard DPA pages.

POC plan: 2-week dedicated POC in Redwood staging with QLT production traces; Run three scenarios — steady-state, market-open burst, noisy-neighbor injection. SE to provide test harness + results deck.
Commercial ask: committed capacity discount tiers, burst-to-hosted pricing model, and explicit SLA credits for latency violations. Procurement expects ELA template by next meeting.
Internal notes: infra team debated L40 vs A100; platform asks for smarter routing policy (per-route token buckets + priority queueing). SE recommended traffic-shaping doc v2.
Next internal owners: AE Mariana to drive contract, SE Ethan to run POC, CSM Lena to prepare onboarding checklist if closed.
Potential upsell: Redwood Optimize to recommend batching/quantization profiles after POC to reduce unit costs on background workloads.
